explanations: In BoundedPool.run, `this.active--` only executes on the success path. When a task rejects (e.g. an inventory reserve times out), the catch branch rejects the caller but never decrements `active`. Each failure permanently leaks a slot; after `concurrency` failures `active` stays at the limit, drain() never starts anything, queued work piles up until maxQueued, and every new order gets PoolSaturatedError. The decrement belongs in a finally block (or before both branches).

Each submit pushes onto the queue and calls drain(), which starts jobs only while active < concurrency, so 8 run and 12 wait. The limit is per pool instance, shared by all orders, not per order. Saturation only happens when the queue length reaches maxQueued (500). drain() does not await run(); it fires it and keeps looping.

The branch `failedSkus.length > 0 && reservations.length > 0` submits release calls for each reservation through the pool and returns `reservations: []` with the failed SKUs, making the order all-or-nothing. It does not return partial reservations, does not throw in this branch, and contains no retry.

Promise.all would reject on the first failure while other reserves are still in flight, so the service would not learn which reservations succeeded and could not release them. allSettled waits for all outcomes. It does not affect concurrency (the pool does), does not retry, and Promise.all cannot cancel underlying requests.
